title: Alcohol use disorder: severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's alcohol use, if any is reportable.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for alcohol use.

Vitals: BP 138/88, HR 76, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or weight changes.
HEENT: Negative for vision changes or ear pain.
Respiratory: Negative for cough or shortness of breath.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for abdominal pain.
Neurological: Negative for tremors or numbness.
Psychiatric: Positive for anxiety.

HPI: (Copied Forward) Patient is a 78-year-old male presenting for follow-up regarding his alcohol consumption. He reports regular daily intake. He expresses a desire to decrease his consumption but notes difficulty with self-regulation.

Update: The patient reports that he is currently drinking. He admits to consuming several drinks daily despite previous goals to reduce intake. He denies any new physical symptoms but notes increased anxiety regarding his consumption habits.

Medication List:
1. Lisinopril 10mg daily
2. Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears well-nourished.
Psychiatric: Cooperative, slightly anxious.
Integumentary: No significant skin lesions.

Assessment:
1. Alcohol use disorder, severe.

Plan:
1. Discussed the severity of his current consumption.
2. Provided education on harm reduction and support groups.
3. Patient will attend a local community support meeting twice weekly.
4. Follow up in two weeks.

Electronically signed, R. Mensah, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Alcohol use disorder, moderate or severe, indexes to alcohol dependence: F10.20 (HCC 139).

distractors.why: Moderate or severe use disorder is dependence (F10.2-); abuse has no HCC.
A use disorder with a severity is documented.

hccs.label: Alcohol Use Disorder/Moderate/Severe/Alcohol Use with Specified Non-Psychotic Complications
